is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles arabiensis in western Kenya (page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports Vgsc L995S (referred to as L1014S) in An. gambiae and An. arabiensis (Table 2, page 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides genotype counts (LL, LS, SS) for L1014S in seven populations for both An. gambiae and An. arabiensis (page 6).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from seven villages in western Kenya (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study evaluating insecticidal decay and resistance in field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies seven villages: Iguhu, Emakakha, Chulaimbo, Emutete, Bungoma, Ahero, and Kisian (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was published in 2015, and the methods describe field collections and bioassays conducted for this specific study (page 3-4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections and bioassays conducted by the authors.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and site locations, are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the insecticidal decay of LLINs and IRS (lambda-cyhalothrin) in seven villages in western Kenya. It assessed the susceptibility of field-collected An. gambiae and An. arabiensis to pyrethroids and genotyped the L1014S kdr mutation. The study found high levels of resistance and significant kdr mutation frequencies, particularly in An. gambiae.
